findings_addressed: TC-133 (§3a, HITL ruling 2026-07-30 / steward seq-212 option (b) / todos-ledger seq-197): scripts/check-board-currency.sh exited 0 on a board whose HAND-WRITTEN rows contradicted dev/plans/release-state-<ver>.json, because the only board predicate was 'does the landing merge's short SHA appear SOMEWHERE in the file'. In the real incident STATUS-0.8.20.md said Slice 39 was NOT_STARTED while 91db34d8 was present — but only inside the two <!-- BEGIN GENERATED --> cells. The generated half was carrying the check for the hand-written half; the always-on CI job passed too. FIXED by a new step 6, the board/state cross-read.

Step 6 checks four things per live board with a readable state file: (a) every id in `landed` has a row in the board's ladder table; (b) that row carries no not-started / in-flight / next marker; (c) that row cites the slice's own `ladder[].sha` — in the ROW, not merely somewhere in the file; (d) every `Ladder remaining:` / `Remaining ladder:` claim names exactly the ids in `remaining_ladder`.

Step 6 runs UNCONDITIONALLY, including for a board that already failed steps 3-5. Git ancestry and the single writer are independent questions; reporting only the first would hide the second, which is a large part of how this defect survived.

SELF-INFLICTED false negative caught before it shipped: the first draft of the (d) claim reader cut the clause at the first punctuation mark. Graded against a matrix (not one example) it read `Ladder remaining: 39.5, 40` as {39.5} — silently dropping every id after the comma — and truncated `40.5` to `40` at the `.`, i.e. re-introduced this very unit's defect class inside the fix for it. Replaced with an ID-LIST reader. Fixtures P (agreeing comma+fractional claim, must stay green) and Q (claim omits 39.5, must go red) pin both directions.

determine_marker_detection.duty: §3a [DETERMINE]: whether the not-started / in-flight / next marker detection should be a FIXED VOCABULARY or DERIVED — state the choice and why; then say plainly what a prose regex can and cannot catch.
determine_marker_detection.determination: FIXED VOCABULARY, explicitly listed in one place in scripts/check-board-currency.sh (STATE_MARKERS + WHOLE_CELL_MARKERS).
why_not_derived: There is nothing to derive it FROM. dev/plans/release-state-<ver>.json only ever authors POSITIVE status (`ladder[].status` = LANDED / NOT_STARTED); it carries no field enumerating words that mean 'not done'. Deriving the negative set as the complement of the positive one means deriving it from open-ended English — unbounded and unfalsifiable.

The one plausible derivation — 'reuse the `ladder[].status` values the state file currently assigns to NON-landed slices' — is SELF-WEAKENING: that set empties out exactly when every slice is landed, i.e. at the end of a release, which is precisely when a board is most likely to be stale. A check that evaporates when it matters is the vacuous-pass family the fix-1 guard exists to end.
It could also only ever contain the STATE FILE's vocabulary, never the BOARD's prose vocabulary — but the board's prose is the thing under test.
A fixed list is auditable: its gaps are visible in one place, and widening it is a deliberate, reviewable act.

vocabulary.why_next_is_whole_cell_only: A bare \bnext\b was REJECTED after grading a matrix. In a status cell 'next' is overwhelmingly a POINTER word ('carried to the next slice', 'closed; next is Slice 40', 'LANDED; the next commission is SLICE-ID-HARDENING') rather than a STATE word, and this gate runs inside `preflight.sh --landing` and the always-on CI job — a false positive here HARD-BLOCKS A LAND. Fixture N's Slice 5 row deliberately reads '… (merge). Carried to the next unit.' and must stay green; it does. Measured cost of the narrowing: a board writing 'next in queue' for a landed slice is NOT caught by (b) — it is caught by (c).

determine_marker_detection.what_the_regex_CANNOT_catch: Any wording not on the list. 'pending', 'TBD', 'queued', 'blocked on X', 'awaiting review', '0/5 arms green', an em-dash, an EMPTY cell, or a row that is simply months out of date while using upbeat words — ALL PASS check (b). It is a prose regex: it detects the phrasings someone thought of, and every board that goes stale in a NEW phrasing goes stale silently as far as (b) is concerned. All of these were run through the matrix and confirmed to pass unflagged.
determine_marker_detection.what_the_regex_FALSELY_catches: The state markers match ANYWHERE in the status cell, so a landed slice whose close prose says 'closed while in-flight work was parked', or 'R-20-PR/R-20-EAV/TC-33 not started; now shipped' (a real phrasing, at STATUS-0.8.20.md:316 in a different table), IS flagged. That is the intended strictness — a landed slice's own status cell should not contain those words — but it costs a land-blocking hard failure, so it is stated in the code rather than discovered later.
determine_marker_detection.which_half_to_trust: (c) — 'the ladder row must cite the slice's own recorded landing SHA' — is the LOAD-BEARING half: it is derived from the state file, has NO vocabulary at all, and is the check that would actually have caught the real Slice 39 incident. (b) is the FRAGILE half and is documented as such in-code. An over-trusted partial check is how this defect class survives, so the code says outright which half is which.
determine_marker_detection.scope_is_structural_not_prose: The check reads only (i) the board's ladder TABLE, located by its own header row `| Slice | … | Status |` plus the markdown delimiter row beneath it, and (ii) `Ladder remaining:` / `Remaining ladder:` claims. Never a section heading, never a whole-file grep. That is what keeps historical close-record prose out of scope (STATUS-0.8.20.md:1002/1011 deliberately retain stale 'NOT STARTED' wording as history) and what keeps OTHER `| 22 | … |` tables out (:316 is an HITL-DECISION row numbered 22 whose text contains 'not started'; reading it as Slice 22's status would be a land-blocking false positive). A duplicate slice id across ladder rows is refused rather than last-writer-wins, mirroring check-release-state-views.sh `_by_slice`.

absent_or_unparseable_state_file_policy.problem: The gate loops over EVERY live STATUS-0.8.z.md board (the board-discovery loop and the `ver=` derivation), not just 0.8.20. Only 0.8.20 has a dev/plans/release-state-<ver>.json — the single writer arrived with DOC-HYGIENE-2 T2a. A hard fail on absence would redden the real gate for unrelated boards; a silent skip would re-create the blind spot being closed.
absent_or_unparseable_state_file_policy.absent: SKIP the cross-read, and SAY SO. stderr carries: `note   <ver>: no dev/plans/release-state-<ver>.json — the board/state cross-read (TC-133) DID NOT RUN for this board; only the git-ancestry SHA check vouched for it…`. Not a failure. Visible in `preflight.sh --landing` output too (preflight routes non-STALE lines through `info` with a `board-currency:` prefix).
absent_or_unparseable_state_file_policy.present_but_unparseable: HARD fail. 'Unparseable' = not valid JSON, OR not a JSON object, OR missing any of `landed` / `ladder` / `remaining_ladder`, OR unreadable (OSError). Message: `STALE  <ver>: … could not be read as release state (<err>) — the board/state cross-read (TC-133) cannot vouch for <board>`. Rationale: that release DOES declare a single writer, so falling back to the SHA-only predicate would be exactly the silent vacuous pass this step closes — the same family as the fix-1 guard.
absent_or_unparseable_state_file_policy.no_ladder_table_in_a_board_that_HAS_a_st: HARD fail — the cross-read would vouch for nothing.
absent_or_unparseable_state_file_policy.no_Ladder_remaining_claim_in_the_board: Visible `note` line saying that half vouched for nothing; not a failure (the (a)/(b)/(c) checks still ran).
absent_or_unparseable_state_file_policy.python3_absent: HARD fail with an explicit message. python3 embedded in a bash gate is this repo's house style (commission-manifest.sh, check-release-state-views.sh); bash cannot read JSON without inventing a parser.

self_inflicted_defects_caught_before_shi.description: The obvious (d) implementation cut the `Ladder remaining:` clause at the first punctuation mark. Graded on a matrix rather than one example, it read `Ladder remaining: 39.5, 40` as {39.5} (comma-separated ladders are the natural way to write a two-slice remainder) and would have truncated `40.5` to `40` at the `.` — this unit's own defect class, re-introduced inside the fix for it.
self_inflicted_defects_caught_before_shi.resolution: Replaced with an ID-LIST reader that consumes ids and separators (whitespace, `*`, backtick, `,`, `;`, `&`, `+`, `→`, `->`, `and`) and stops at the first non-id word ('alone', 'then', 'NONE'). Fixtures P and Q added; both directions armed. Matches the brief's warning that both prior legs' one-line [DETERMINE] fixes introduced a new false negative.

self_inflicted_defects_caught_before_shi.description: A bare `\bnext\b` marker — the literal reading of 'next marker' — false-positives on legitimate close prose ('carried to the next slice') in a gate that hard-blocks landing.
self_inflicted_defects_caught_before_shi.resolution: Narrowed to whole-cell `next` / `next up` / `up next`, with the narrowing and its cost stated in-code and pinned by fixture N, whose Slice 5 row reads '… Carried to the next unit.' and must stay green.

out_of_scope_reported_not_fixed: The check-release-state-views.sh generated cells inside STATUS-0.8.20.md are the mechanism by which the SHA reached the file while the hand-written half stayed wrong. Making the RENDERED half and the HAND-WRITTEN half structurally impossible to disagree (e.g. rendering the ladder table itself) is a real option and is NOT in this leg's scope; the gate now merely detects the disagreement.

check (b)'s vocabulary gap is real and permanent: 'pending', 'TBD', 'queued', 'blocked on X', an empty cell, and any month-old-but-upbeat wording all pass. Closing it properly needs a positive contract on what a LANDED row must say, not a longer list of what it must not. Reported, not attempted.
